canonical_topic: Bond Prices Move Inversely to Interest Rates
definition: A future payment is economically equivalent to a bond, and bond prices move opposite to interest rates: bonds are more valuable when rates are low and less valuable when rates are high. The market trading interest rates is called the Bond Market or Fixed Income market.
core_idea: Because any future cash flow behaves like a bond, forward/future energy contracts carry an implicit interest-rate sensitivity tied to the discounting of that future payment.
key_points: Future payments are treated as economically equivalent to bonds.
Bond prices and interest rates move in opposite directions.
The interest-rate market is called the Bond Market or Fixed Income market.
relationships: Connects to Forward vs Future Contracts, since forwards/futures involve payments at a future date.
trading_implications: Valuing a forward or future contract implicitly involves discounting a future payment, so interest-rate moves affect contract value independent of the underlying commodity price.
